requirements.reason: AdminAction persistence requires a registered action, explicit finite outcome, canonical correlation UUID, valid typed target, authenticated actor, and database-owned time.
PostgreSQL must reject row updates and deletes for both administrative audit tables with one stable append-only error while schema-owner truncation remains available for test cleanup.
Corrections append an immutable self-linked action in a private transaction, replay idempotently, and cannot form correction chains.
The ordinary writer never commits and its failure rolls back the privileged mutation in the caller-owned transaction.

The reusable sensitive-read recorder reauthorizes in a private session, validates only minimal target projections, commits before disclosure, accepts no protected payload, and fails closed without disturbing caller state.
Audit correlation is copied from trusted context and legitimate non-request recording generates and installs a fresh canonical UUIDv4.
All audit read surfaces and service entry points enforce binary active-admin access, preserve private no-store behavior and retired mutations, and expose additive outcome/correlation data safely.
Every existing production writer uses the explicit outcome and database-time contract, and commit-owning checkpoint workflows use immutable typed relationships instead of rewriting audit rows.
